title: StrazzTunedBuddy
tagline: An open-source driving companion for your car
summary: A little expressive companion that sits on your dashboard: an Arduino Nano driving a 128x64 OLED, cycling through moods — regular blinking eyes, heart eyes, side-eye, and a sleep state. Inspired by the Dasai Mochi, but fully open source, so anyone can build one for the cost of a microcontroller and a screen.
highlights: The most-starred and most-forked project on my GitHub, built and shared entirely as open hardware.
Every expression is drawn procedurally from primitives — no sprite sheets or bitmap assets — so the whole firmware is a single readable file.
Published with a full parts list, wiring guide, and a companion 3D-printable case so the build is genuinely reproducible.
methodology: Drove the display with the Adafruit SSD1306 and GFX libraries over I2C on an Arduino Nano.
Composed each facial expression from GFX primitives (filled rectangles, circles, and triangles) and animated them by redrawing the framebuffer between timed delays.
Randomised the expression selection in the main loop so the companion feels reactive rather than looping predictably.
Documented the hardware bill of materials and wiring so the project could be forked and built by others — which it has been, 19 times.

gallery.caption: regEyes — the default idle loop, round eyes with a blink
heart — heart-shaped eyes above a rounded smile
carrotEyes — angled chevron eyes with a smile
sideEye — blinking while the eyes shift wider apart
sleep — closed eyes and a small mouth
wakeUp — the winking sequence played on power-on

galleryNote: These are not mockups: the firmware's own drawing calls were interpreted and rasterised at the device's real 128x64 resolution and frame timings, so each loop is exactly what the OLED displays.
